title: CLAY COUNTY PROPERTY TAXES
full_story:
Clay County Real Estate tax bills were mailed on September 11th.

The first installment of the 2025 taxes payable in 2026 is due on Friday, October 16th.  The second installment is due on Friday, November 20th.

Payment can be made to the Clay County Treasurer using any of the following options, by mail, send your check with the payment stub to the Clay County Treasurer PO Box 88 Louisville, IL 62858.  Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date to avoid penalty.  You can pay at the treasurer’s office in the Clay County Courthouse where they accept cash, checks, cashier’s checks, or money orders.  Please bring your entire bill if you want it stamped to show proof of payment.  Office hours are 8:00 am – 4:00 pm Monday through Friday.  Online payments can be made by credit/debit card by going to govpaynow.com PLC #a00082, there will be a convenience fee charged for online Credit Card payments.  Payment can also be made by placing your payment in the envelope depository at the north entrance of the Clay County Courthouse.  Please include payment stub.

For questions call Clay County Treasurer Stacey Allen’s office at 618-665-3727.

title: BLOOD DRIVE TOMORROW
full_story:
The American Red Cross is appealing for blood and platelet donors of all blood types to schedule donation appointments this fall.  The organization provides more than 6.5 million blood products to hospitals nationwide each year.

There will be a Blood Drive tomorrow at the Flora Church of the Nazarene from Noon to 5 pm.  Donors who give blood or platelets before October 18th will receive a $15 e-gift card to a merchant of their choice.

To be eligible to donate, individuals must be at least 17 years old, or 16 with parental consent, where permitted by state law and weigh at least 110 pounds while in generally good health.  High school students and other donors 18 years of age and younger must also meet specific height and weight requirements.  Donors must present a blood donor card, driver’s license or two other forms of identification at check-in.

Appointments can be made using the Red Cross Blood Donor App, by visiting RedCrossBlood.org, by calling 1-800-RED CROSS or by enabling the Blood Donor Skill on Alexa Echo devices.  Donors can use RapidPass online on the day of their appointment to complete pre-donation reading and health history questionnaires before arriving.

The next Blood Drive in our area will be on Thursday, October 29th at the Clay City High School from 1 to 5 pm.

title: ALTAMONT MAN INJURED
full_story:
Bryan Baker, 49, of Altamont was injured in a single-vehicle crash in Liberty Township, in Effingham County on Monday afternoon.

The Effingham County Sheriff’s office reported that a vehicle operated by Baker was traveling south on 300th street at 3:53 pm. Approximately a quarter mile south of State Highway 33 negotiating the S-curves in the roadway.  A deer entered the roadway, and Baker swerved to miss the deer, causing him to lose control and strike the guardrail head-on on the east side of the roadway.

Baker was treated by Rural Med EMS, and later transported to St. Anthony’s Hospital.

title: SANTA SMILES APPLICATIONS
full_story:
Applications for Santa Smiles for this year are now available.

Applications can be picked up at the Clay City Village Hall, Xenia Village Hall, Louisville Village Hall, Louisville Banking Company, or Salt & Strings Butchery.  In Flora applications are available at the Flora City Hall, Flora Library, CEFS, and the office of Todd Fender at the Clay County Housing Authority.  The Clay County Health Department will give their applications to their clients.

Applications are due on November 1st and can be dropped off at the Clay City Village Hall, Louisville Village Hall, and Xenia City Hall.  In Flora Applications can be dropped off at the Clay County Housing authority night drop box.  Applications can also be mailed.

Santa Smiles will also have a Christmas Auction on Friday, October 23rd at 6 pm at the Xenia Community Center.  Santa Smiles is providing concessions at the auction.

Last year Santa Smiles provided gifts to 523 kids, and 71 residents at Chestnut Corner Sheltered Care in Louisville.

title: STORM SPOTTER TRAINING
full_story:
The Effingham County Emergency Management Agency in collaboration with the National Weather Service in Lincoln will be holding a Special Storm Spotter Training Class on Saturday, October 24th, from 10 am to Noon at the Effingham County Emergency Operations Center, 311 Miracle Avenue, Effingham.

During the regular storm spotter training, participants will learn the characteristics of severe thunderstorms and other associated threats, severe weather-relevant cloud formations, and weather safety practices.

Participants will also learn how they can be a National Weather Service SKYWARN volunteer and help keep their community safe, by providing timely and accurate reports of severe weather directly to the National Weather Service.

In addition to the usual storm spotter training, the NWS is providing a winter storm outlook with safety information, and the NWS will also explain ways they provide incident support to first responders.

The class is free and open to the public and pre-registration is NOT required.

For questions about the training, please call Effingham County Emergency Management Agency, 217-540-1669.

title: MOBILE DMV RECORD
full_story:
Illinois Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias announced that the office’s Mobile DMV program has surpassed 60,000 transactions, bringing essential driver and vehicle services directly to communities across Illinois.

Since January of 2023, the Secretary of State’s office has held more than 1,700 Mobile DMV events, completing more than 62,000 transactions.  Among those transactions, Mobile DMV operations have issued more than 50,000 REAL IDs, driver’s licenses and state IDs.  Mobile operations have also completed 2,600 road tests and processed more than 8,500 vehicle registration sticker transactions.

“Since taking office, we have worked to make the DMV more convenient and accessible for Illinois residents,” said Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias.  “Mobile DMV events allow us to bring essential services directly to communities, saving residents time and making it easier to take care of their DMV needs.  This is another example of how we are rethinking the way government delivers services to the people of Illinois.”

Some Mobile DMV events utilize the Secretary of State’s self-contained DMV on Wheels units, which are equipped with onboard internet, allowing for quick setup at designated locations.  Other pop-up events are held at community locations without the use of a Mobile DMV vehicle.

The Secretary of State’s office works with municipalities, organizations, businesses, universities and other community partners to host Mobile DMV events and bring services closer to residents.  The Mobile DMV units also provide the office with greater flexibility to quickly establish service at a designated location when needed to avoid any disruption in service for customers.

title: TO ELECT 3 NEW MEMBERS
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Agriculture (IDOA) announced an election will be held on October 28th, for two board members in the following Illinois Wheat Development Board Districts (IWDB) three and six as well as one (1) statewide At-Large Board Member.  District six includes Clay, Wayne, Alexander, Edwards, Gallatin, Hamilton, Hardin, Johnson, Massac, Pope, Pulaski, Saline, Union, Wabash, White, Williamson Counties.  As no formal petitions were filed for these vacant board positions, producers of Illinois wheat residing in these Districts may participate in the October 28th, election as a write-in candidate.  Producers must be of legal voting age, reside in the district for which they are running and be a qualified producer of wheat.  At-large write-in candidates may reside in any of the IWDB Districts.

Absentee ballots are available to those not available to vote in person by contacting IDOA at 217-524-1083 or by email at agr.marketnews.illinois.gov.  In-person voting will take place at the county Farm Bureau offices in Illinois during normal business hours.

For more information, call IDOA at (217) 524-1083 or the Illinois Wheat Association at (309) 557-3619.

title: CYBERSECURITY MONTH
full_story:
Experts are stressing the importance of caution and vigilance during Cybersecurity Month.

James Mayer, founder and CEO of Mayer Networks, says people and businesses should focus on recognizing potential breaches and limiting the damage when they occur.

“Cybersecurity is not about preventing the breach or stopping it from happening.  It’s about identifying that it is happening and then having the controls in place to stop it, mitigate it, and especially with businesses get them back to working shape as soon as we can.”

Using strong, unique passwords and turning on multi-factor authentication can help protect online accounts.  Experts also recommend being cautious of suspicious emails, text messages and links, keeping devices and apps updated, and regularly checking bank accounts for unusual activity.

Mayer says having reliable backups is especially important for businesses in the event their systems are compromised.

Experts also warn that artificial intelligence is making scams more convincing.  They recommend taking a moment to verify unexpected messages before clicking links or sharing personal information.

The bottom line: stay alert, monitor your accounts and think twice before clicking.
